title: Are Mount Denali and Mount Kilimanjaro very different in height?
description: The heights of Mount Denali and Mount Kilimanjaro are in the table, and a short count up from the smaller height shows how far apart they are. Keeko doubts this and says they are very different because one is in the six thousands and the other in the five thousands.
teaching_notes: One idea: to see whether two heights are very different, find how far apart they are and compare that with the heights themselves. Watch for students who judge only by the first digit.

source: Are Mount Denali and Mount Kilimanjaro very different in height?
video_script.why: The child reads two close heights from the table and finds how far apart they are, which a table of numbers does not show at a glance.
video_script.substitution: The heights of two mountains of the table of the book are compared by counting up.
video_script.anchor: the table of the tallest mountain on each continent, with the heights of Mount Denali and Mount Kilimanjaro lit
video_script.wrong_answer: six thousand is more than five thousand
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko looks only at the first digits, 6 thousand and 5 thousand, and calls the mountains very different. The two heights are only 299 m apart, which is small for mountains close to 6000 m high, so the claim is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: They differ by only two hundred and ninety nine metres, so they are not very different

final_answer.value: No, they differ by only 299 m.
final_answer.spoken: no, they differ by only two hundred and ninety nine metres

maths_rules: Mount Denali is 6194 m, Mount Kilimanjaro is 5895 m
count up from the smaller: 5895 to 5900 is 5 m
299 m is small beside heights near 6000 m, so the mountains are not very different
video_script.design: The table of the book is hard to read at a glance, so the two heights are lit and counted up from the smaller one in two jumps. The total distance is compared with the heights themselves.

<bookmark mark='table'/>A large table of numbers is slow to read.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Mount Denali is six thousand one hundred and ninety four metres high. Mount Kilimanjaro is five thousand eight hundred and ninety five metres high.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Are these two mountains very different in height?

narration: <bookmark mark='line'/>To see how different two heights are, we look at the gap between them.
<bookmark mark='gap'/>We find the gap by counting up from the smaller height to the greater.

<bookmark mark='jump'/>Count up to the next hundred, five thousand nine hundred. That jump is five metres.

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step two, from five thousand nine hundred to six thousand is one hundred metres.
<bookmark mark='second'/>From six thousand to six thousand one hundred and ninety four is one hundred and ninety four metres.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>One hundred and one hundred and ninety four make two hundred and ninety four metres.

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>They differ by only two hundred and ninety nine metres, so they are not very different.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Check by adding back. The smaller height plus the gap gives the greater height.

narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks six thousand is more than five thousand, so the mountains are very different.
<bookmark mark='bars'/>But Keeko looked only at the first digits. The two bars are almost equal.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The gap is only two hundred and ninety nine metres, so the mountains are not very different.
